environment.description: Same Rails application code deployed as a container image invoked behind an AWS Lambda function URL. The function URL is configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda function URL resource policy specifies a principal condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID) restricting invocation to identities within the organization's AWS accounts. The Lambda function URL does NOT support WebSocket upgrade (HTTP/1.1 Upgrade header is stripped by the Lambda invoke proxy; Lambda function URLs only support request-response HTTP semantics via the Lambda Runtime API). Additionally, the function URL's invoke mode is set to BUFFERED (not RESPONSE_STREAM), meaning the connection is terminated after a single request-response cycle. The /cable mount path returns a 426 Upgrade Required from Rails but the WebSocket handshake never completes because the Lambda function URL proxy does not maintain persistent connections or pass through the 101 Switching Protocols response.

config.infrastructure: AWS Lambda function URL (container image runtime)
config.connection_semantics: Request-response only, no persistent connections, HTTP Upgrade not proxied
config.iam_auth_enforcement: Unauthenticated requests receive 403 Forbidden before reaching application code
